basis: Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; encephalopathy and intrinsic myopathy commonly affect >30% across the group; cardiac and hepatic involvement varies.
Progressive intrinsic proximal muscle degeneration defines calpainopathy; cardiac involvement is characteristically absent.
Cellular or antibody-mediated immune injury to a graft; no specific transplanted organ is specified.
Corticospinal tract degeneration defines pure spastic paraplegia; muscle atrophy and urinary dysfunction are neurogenic, without independent muscle or urinary tract disease.
Malignant mesenchymal tumour arising predominantly in deep soft tissues or bone; nonspecific peritoneal annotations do not establish common gastrointestinal damage.
Calculus within a urinary bladder diverticulum; the urinary bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Pancreatic epithelial adenoma; no islet-cell origin or endocrine dysfunction is specified.
Congenital glycosylation defect with a defining epileptic phenotype including infantile spasms; pigmentation changes alone do not establish damaging skin involvement.
Immune/platelet defects and visual albinism define CHS; progressive neurologic dysfunction affects most long-term survivors. Cap omits skin, frequent hepatic and periodontal involvement.
Creatine biosynthesis defect defined clinically by developmental disability, seizures and movement abnormalities; hypotonia does not establish intrinsic myopathy.
IgG4-related multifocal fibrosis; retroperitoneal ureteric encasement commonly causes obstructive urinary dysfunction (>30%); other organ sites vary.
Retinal dystrophy, sensorineural deafness and renal Fanconi dysfunction define the syndrome; phosphate-wasting rickets affects 4/6 patients.
Congenital lymphatic lesion occupies the larynx, an upper-airway structure; dysphagia does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
Inherited peripheral vestibular disorder causing recurrent vertigo; vestibular dysfunction belongs to the otologic axis.
Carcinoma originates in minor salivary glands of the oral cavity, both included in the gastrointestinal axis.
Placental gestational trophoblastic disease lies outside the axes; blood-loss anemia is a separately diagnosed complication and hyperthyroidism occurs in <30%.
Profound deafness and hand contractures define the syndrome; lacrimal duct atresia and blepharophimosis occur in 80-99%, supporting ocular involvement.
Definition specifies existing cutaneous dysplastic nevi; melanoma susceptibility does not establish damage in any additional organ.
Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia is an IgM-producing lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma involving marrow; additional organ damage is not consistently common.
Specified defining features are intellectual disability and cleft palate; short stature and unusual facies alone do not establish another damaged organ.
Bilateral opercular corticobulbar dysfunction causes pseudobulbar paralysis; dysphagia and facial weakness are neurologic manifestations.
Inherited cardiac electrical disease causing ventricular tachycardia, fibrillation and cardiac arrest; no independent extracardiac disease is established.
Benign epithelial neoplasm of the bronchus or lung; pulmonary origin is explicit in the definition.
Inflammation of small-intestinal diverticula; nonspecific inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated disease.
Accessory breast tissue is a breast developmental anomaly; breast tissue is outside the 13 axes.
